jobs.description:
Do you want to establish an independent research programme in infectious diseases, immunology or microbiology? At CIMM, you will have protected time, strong support and an outstanding scientific environment to become an internationally visible research leader. As an Assistant Professor on the CIMM tenure track, you will establish and lead an innovative, independent and sustainable research programme in infectious diseases, immunology or microbiology. Your programme may focus on acute infections and/or post-acute infection syndromes, should complement and strengthen CIMM's portfolio, and may be fun_amental, translational or combine both approaches. Clinical research and structural clinical duties are outside the scope of this position. The indicative allocation of duties is 80% research, 10% teaching and 10% academic leadership, management, outreach and societal engagement. Define and deliver an ambitious research strategy, covering the full research cycle from formulating questions and designing studies to translating findings into scientific and societal impact; Build national and international collaborations and strengthen your international scientific visibility; Obtain competitive external funding as principal investigator or co-principal investigator and publish rigorous, impactful research; Recruit, supervise and mentor PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers, research staff and _tudents; Contribute to teaching, academic leadership, team science, Open Science, knowledge sharing, societal engagement and CIMM's collaborative research culture. You are a collaborative and ambitious researcher who is ready to take the next step towards independent research leadership. You bring: A PhD in infectious diseases, immunology, microbiology or a closely related biomedical, medical or life-sciences field, followed by relevant postdoctoral research experience; A strong scientific track record appropriate to your career stage, a clear and original research vision and

evidence of increasing scientific independence; High-quality peer-reviewed publications demonstrating substantial intellectual contributions, together with experience in competitive grant applications and the potential to build an externally funded research programme; Experience in supervising and mentoring junior researchers and a commitment to high-quality education; a Basic Teaching Qualification (BKO) is welcome but not required at the time of appointment; Strong communication and leadership skills, excellent spoken and written English and the ability to contribute to a collaborative, inclusive and safe research environment. International research experience and an established collaborative network are considered assets. One-year contract with the prospect of a permanent contract. Keep a high-tech factory moving In a high-tech manufacturing environment, having the right material available at the right moment is essential. A missing component, delayed delivery or unreliable supplier can directly impact production. As an Operational Buyer, you will take responsibility for the operational purchasing process and the availability of materials and components. Suppliers and commercial agreements are already in place; your focus is on making sure purchase orders are executed correctly, deliveries arrive as promised and potential supply issues are addressed before they impact the factory. This is a hands-on role where you will be in direct contact with suppliers and work closely with planning, manufacturing and logistics. You will monitor the supply situation, manage changing priorities and take ownership when deliveries or material availability are at risk. Your work will include: Managing and following up on purchase orders for technical materials and components. Monitoring delivery performance and acting when suppliers are at risk of missing agreed lead times. Maintaining direct contact with suppliers regarding order status, delays and delivery commitments. Coordinating material availability with planning and manufacturing teams. Taking ownership of shortages, supply disruptions and other operational issues until they are resolved. Escalating critical supply issues and coordinating actions with the right internal and external stakeholders. Making operational purchasing decisions based on lead times, delivery requirements and costs. Identifying recurring supply issues and contributing to structural improvements. Maintaining accurate purchasing and material data in SAP or another ERP system. Arbeidsvoorwaarden A gross monthly salary between €3,600 and €5,100, excluding holiday allowance. 25 vacation days, excluding public holidays, plus 13 ADV days. Pension scheme and travel allowance. A personal development and growth plan. Opportunities to furthe

develop yourself within purchasing, supply chain and high-tech manufacturing. A dynamic and international working environment. Free lunch or dinner at the location. You will take ownership of the purchasing process and work closely with suppliers, planning, manufacturing and logistics to ensure materials and components are available when needed. It is a hands-on position with plenty of responsibility and variety. You will develop your experience in operational purchasing, supplier management and supply chain coordination while working with complex technical products and an international supplier network. The role also offers plenty of opportunities to grow within a large and technologically advanced organization, where different engineering and supply chain disciplines work closely together.
